title: ES-01 regression: rate-dilution griefing still reachable via unguarded claim() / stake() / unstake() entry points
description: The story-003 fix added the `ownerOrNotGriefed` modifier to `topUp` and `pullAndRefresh` to stop non-owner callers from re-calling the budget sync when it would reduce `rewardRate`. However the modifier is NOT applied to the three user-facing entry points that also invoke `_syncBudget()` internally: `stake()`, `unstake()`, and `claim()`. `claim()` in particular does not require the caller to have any prior stake or pending reward — if `user.amount == 0`, `pending == 0` and the whole body is a no-op after `_syncBudget`, but `_syncBudget` still executes unconditionally and will happily reset the window / recompute a lower rate from a tiny dispatcher inflow. The entire ES-01 griefing vector from the prior audit therefore survives unchanged, just behind a trivially different entry point. The modifier is a locked front door while the back door (claim with zero stake) is wide open.
economicImpact: Attacker reduces the per-second reward rate paid to legitimate stakers indefinitely, identical to the original ES-01 scenario: every poke extends `windowEnd` back to `now + windowDuration` and re-spreads the still-largely-unspent budget over a fresh full window. Concrete example reused from the prior finding (540-day window, 90e18 phUSD remaining with 90 days to go on the original schedule): original realised rate ~1.157e13 wei/sec; after one poke via `claim()` the new rate is ~(90e18 + dust)/540 days ≈ 1.929e12 wei/sec — an ~83% reduction in the rate stakers earn for the rest of the year. Repeated pokes hold the rate at the diluted level. The `ownerOrNotGriefed` modifier does not observe the rate change because it isn't on the call path.
attackPath:
1. Deploy has some `rewardBudget` and a live window; dispatcher hook is wired and accrues mint-debt continuously (small but non-zero every block).
2. Attacker (ANY EOA — no stake required, not a pauser, not the owner) calls `NFTStaker.claim()`.
3. `whenNotPaused` passes. `_syncBudget()` executes: `_updatePool` settles accrual at OLD rate; `dispatcherHook.pull()` mints X > 0 phUSD to the contract; inflow = X > 0 triggers the reset branch; `windowEnd = now + windowDuration`, `rewardRate = rewardBudget / windowDuration` (lower than before).
4. `user.amount == 0` → `pending == 0` → no transfer. `user.rewardDebt` is reset to 0. Function returns successfully.
5. `ownerOrNotGriefed` is never evaluated — it is not on `claim()`. No revert, no cost beyond gas.
6. Repeat whenever the dispatcher has accumulated any non-zero mint-debt (i.e. most blocks).
7. Same attack via `stake(1)` (requires owning 1 unit of the staked ERC1155, which anyone can buy) or `unstake(1)` (only by existing stakers).
quantifiedLoss: Worst case identical to original ES-01: realised emission rate collapses to (budget + dust)/windowDuration and stays there. In the 540-day / 90e18-remaining-with-90-days-left example, stakers lose ~83% of their expected forward-emission rate. Because the attack costs only gas (~50k per claim call) and can be repeated every ~12 seconds, the rate can be pinned at the diluted level indefinitely.
recommendation: Move the griefing defence out of the modifier and into `_syncBudget` itself, so every caller (user entry points included) is protected: before applying the reset branch, compute the tentative new rate and only accept the reset when new rate >= old rate OR the prior window has expired. Owner-initiated lower-rate extensions can still be supported by routing them through a new `ownerForceRefresh()` that bypasses the rate-floor. The current layout — modifier on two callers, raw call from three more — is structurally fragile; the defence must live at the sync site, not at individual entry points.
affectedParties: All existing stakers lose forward emission value; late/JIT stakers benefit from the back-loaded budget.
profitability: Profitable to any party that prefers back-loaded emissions (e.g. a planned-late-entry whale) or that simply wants to deny legitimate stakers their yield. Cost is ~50k gas per poke; benefit is the full diluted-vs-original rate differential times remaining stake-weight of the attacker's position (or the attacker's counter-party positions).
